subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram channel can be wedged by bad persisted session JSON; status should detect and offer recovery

question: What recovery contract should OpenClaw use when Telegram or channel status finds a malformed, empty, or oversized session-store artifact?
rationale: Source inspection proves the diagnostic gap, but resetting or quarantining persisted session state can affect continuity and data preservation, so automation should not choose the destructive or self-healing behavior by default.

options.title: Diagnostics First
options.body: Add non-destructive status/doctor detection with file path, size, parse/schema result, and clear backup-then-reset guidance while leaving mutation to an explicit follow-up command.

options.title: Doctor-Owned Repair
options.body: Implement `openclaw doctor --fix` or a channel repair command that backs up and quarantines the bad store before rebuilding or resetting the affected session state.

options.title: Startup Quarantine
options.body: Automatically move bad session-store artifacts aside on load and recreate clean state, accepting the stronger compatibility and data-continuity risk.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics First
recommendation.body: Add non-destructive status/doctor detection with file path, size, parse/schema result, and clear backup-then-reset guidance while leaving mutation to an explicit follow-up command.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history on Telegram status diagnostics and can choose the user-visible recovery contract.
